text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Research by Coopers & Lybrand consultants suggests that Australia's A$175 billion home loan market is being strongly affected by increased refinancing, an increase in the number of loans in arrears and a long-term decline in the number of new home buyers. These forces could have a destabilising affect on the mortgage market. Page 1.

Optus is planning to compete with Telstra in the delivery of communication services to rural Australia with a plan to improve its satellite infrastructure. The plan will see its analog satellite systems switched to digital technology, and will mean pay-TV and Internet services can be offered to all country areas once Australia's telecommunications market opens up in July 1997. Page 1.

Federal backbenchers from Victoria and South Australia, the car industry, business groups and unions are organising a lobbying campaign in the new year against the Productivity Commission's recommendation for a phase-out of protection for the car industry. In a test of how the Coalition balances political pragmatism with its goal for micro-economic reform, backbenchers will argue that a tariff phase-out would be of little national economic benefit and could cost the Government three or four seats in South Australia and some in Victoria. Page 3.

Although Magma copper has achieved a A$47 million profit turnaround in the November quarter, BHP Co Ltd will cut costs by a further 15 per cent at the North American operations to bring it in line with other copper assets. The Magma operations posted a lss of A$30 million for the six months to November 30, compared with a A$222 million profit from the South American operations. Page 13.

Announcing BHP Steel's interim results on Friday, chief executive John Prescott said the group was still examining every option for retaining steel making at its Newcastle works. While BHP Steel's earnings for the November quarter were steady at A$90 milion, Prescott said the one-off effects of blast furnace maintenance at the Newcastle steelworks and redundancy payouts had masked further improvement in the group's earnings. Page 13.

Highlands Gold Ltd yesterday released a summary of independent experts Baring Brothers Burrows' report which valued Highlands at 96 cents-A$1.14 a share - 40 per cent higher than the 75 cents a share offer made by Placer Dome Inc. Highlands managing director Ian Goddard said the valuation showed that Placer's takeover terms completely failed to recognise the value of Highlands' three world-class projects and exploration portfolio. Page 15.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Woodside Petroleum Ltd has chosen ICI Australia Ltd from a pick of international companies to sign a five-year contract to supply the chemical compound to Woodside in its operations in the North West Shelf. The multi-million dollar contract will position ICI for growth in tandem with the North West Shelf consortium. Page 23.

Peter Wills, the chairman of Sydney-based developer CRI, said in a joint statement with construction giant Baulderstone Hornibrook that the two companies will split, with Baulderstone selling its 50 per cent equity stake in CRI, after the companies failed to meet the expectations of their relationship. Page 23.

The reassessment of strategic infrastructure requirements for the next century by a West Australian Government taskforce has left plans to privatise Australia's longest gas-transmission system, the 1600 kilometre Dampier to Bunbury pipeline, under a cloud Page 23.

Advance Bank Ltd shareholders will vote this morning on the controversial St George Bank Ltd merger at a meeting in Sydney. However, even if the merger does receive shareholder approval, there are still legal objections to overcome from the Australian Seurities Commission and the National Australia Bank. Page 24.

Highlands Gold Ltd managing director Ian Goddard said shareholders were yesterday advised to reject Placer Dome Inc's A$423 million takeover offer, after a report by independent company Baring Brother Burrows valued Highlands at A$618 million. Page 25.

The Commonwealth Bank of Australia Ltd's Commonwealth Financial Services arm will be increased by the bank's acquisition of Commonwealth Funds Management Ltd for A$60 million yesterday. The CBA will now be the fourth-biggest money manager in Australia, wth funds under management at A$22 billion. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Leon Davis will be the new chief executive of the A$12 billion RTZ-CRA, the world's largest miner, and he believes the world's uranium market is going to get stronger. This strengthening could see RTZ-CRA make a move to open a new Australian uanium mine, probably in Kintyre in the north of Western Australia. Page 21.

The merger between developer CRI and construction company Baulderstone Hornibrook will end after two years, as it "had not met the expectations of either group". The merger, designed to take on heavy weights Lend Lease and Leighton Holdings, was not, accrding to CRI's chairman Peter Wills, a failure. Page 21.

The St George and Advance Banks are hoping for shareholder support for their proposed A$2.65 billion merger, which is needed to shoot down an Australian Securities Commission legal challenge to the deal. The National Australia Bank is also opposed to the deal. Page 21.

Papua New Guinean gold miner Highlands Gold Ltd's directors have rejected a A$423 million takeover offer from Canadian miner Placer Dome after a report by advisory firm Baring Brothers Burrows valued Highlands at up to A$618 million. Baring concluded tha the Placer bid was not fair nor reasonable. Page 21.

Federal Finance Minister John Fahey yesterday announced the sale of Commonwealth Funds Management to the Commonwealth Bank for A$60 million, double the expected price. Fahey also said CFM's consulting and risk management subsidiary Total Risk Management had been sold to US-based firm Towers Perrin for A$950,000. Page 23.

The Australian Chamber of Manufactures' December 1996 survey of manufacturing found a positive trend in manufacturing for the first time in 21 months. The trends should continue into the March 1997 quarter, allowing for significant growth late in 1997. Page 23.
THE AGE

The A$423 million bid for Highlands Gold by Canadian mining giant Placer Dome was rejected by the Highlands directors at a meeting yesterday. An independent report classed the Placer offer as unfair and not reasonable, placing the value of Highlands in the range of 96 cents a share (A$513 million) to A$1.14 a share (A$618 million), with a mid-point valuation of A$1.05 a share. Page C1.

Melbourne-based company Compumedics, established by former medical electronics engineer David Burton in 1987, is gaining an international reputation for its sleep monitoring equipment, aimed to stop snoring, which is now considered a potentially fatal habit. Page C2.

Department store operator David Jones will be the anchor tenant of New Zealand's new A$400 million Quay Park Mall waterfront shopping complex in Auckland. New Zealand's largest retail development is expected to be completed by September 1999 in time for the America's Cup challenge. Page C3.

A meeting of the United Nations' World Intellectual Property Organisation has agreed to two treaties that will help protect intellectual property from being pirated on the Internet. Negotiators from more than 150 countries agreed to two agreements, one which extends existing international copyright protection of literary and artistic works and a second which provides the first global copyright rules to cover musical recordings. Page C3.

The Federal Court has imposed injunctions restraining two cruise operators in New South Wales' Port Stephens district from making arrangements to fix prices for dolphin-watch cruises, following legal action by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commision. Page C3.

Finance Minister John Fahey announced yesterday that the Federal Government had finalised the sale of Commonwealth Funds Management to the Commonwealth Bank of Australia for A$60 million and had sold Total Risk Management Pty Ltd to Towers Perrin for A$95,000. Page C3.
